burnet:opera:1900.author: Burnet, John (ed.)
burnet:opera:1900.work: Platonis Opera, recognovit brevique adnotatione critica instruxit Ioannes Burnet, Tomi I–V (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1900–1907)
burnet:opera:1900.notes: Authoritative Oxford Classical Text staged verbatim in the Greek (el) track via Perseus Canonical GreekLit TEI-XML.

jowett:dialogues:1892.author: Jowett, Benjamin (trans.)
jowett:dialogues:1892.work: The Dialogues of Plato, Translated into English with Analyses and Introductions, 3rd ed., 5 vols. (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1892)
jowett:dialogues:1892.notes: Public-domain English translation staged in the English (en) track with exact mathematical philology notes.

stephanus:1578.author: Estienne, Henri (Henricus Stephanus, ed.)
stephanus:1578.work: Platonis opera quae extant omnia, 3 vols. (Geneva, 1578)
stephanus:1578.notes: Universal pagination and five-section column standard (a–e) governing all Platonic references.

euclid:elements.author: Euclid of Alexandria
euclid:elements.work: Στοιχεῖα — The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements (ed. Heiberg 1883–1888; trans. Heath 1926)
euclid:elements.notes: Deductive culmination of the fourth-century Academic curriculum (geometor/euclid & geometor/elements).

euclid:I.def.4.author: Euclid
euclid:I.def.4.work: Elements, Book I, Definitions 4 & 15 (Straight Line & Circle)
euclid:I.def.4.notes: Euclidean counterpart to Plato's optical straightness and equidistant roundness in Parmenides 137e.

euclid:I.def.13.author: Euclid
euclid:I.def.13.work: Elements, Book I, Definitions 13–14 & Book XI, Definition 2 (Boundary, Figure & Solid)
euclid:I.def.13.notes: Formalizes Socrates' definition of figure as limit (peras) in Meno 76a.

euclid:I.1.author: Euclid
euclid:I.1.work: Elements, Book I, Proposition 1 (Equilateral Triangle Construction)
euclid:I.1.notes: Constructs the cosmic equilateral face bisected into six Timaeus 1:√3:2 half-triangles.

euclid:I.11.author: Euclid
euclid:I.11.notes: Erects orthogonal legs in Meno's square, Theodorus's spiral, and the Divided Line mean ordinate.

euclid:I.46.author: Euclid
euclid:I.46.work: Elements, Book I, Proposition 46 (Construction of a Square)
euclid:I.46.notes: Constructs the given square ABCD and diagonal square BHKD in Meno 82b–85b.

euclid:I.47.author: Euclid
euclid:I.47.notes: General theorem generalizing Socrates' isosceles case Q = 4 + 4 = 8 and iterating Theodorus's spiral Q_{n+1} = Q_n + 1.

euclid:II.11.author: Euclid
euclid:II.11.work: Elements, Book II, Proposition 11 & Book VI, Proposition 30 (Extreme and Mean Ratio)
euclid:II.11.notes: Canonical Academic 'section' (ἡ τομή) realizing the Divided Line under golden ratio φ.

euclid:II.14.author: Euclid
euclid:II.14.work: Elements, Book II, Proposition 14 & Book VI, Proposition 13 (Quadrature & Mean Proportional)
euclid:II.14.notes: Semicircle ordinate construction of quadratic powers √n (Theaetetus 147d) and geometric mean √(ab) (Timaeus 32a).

euclid:V.def.5.author: Euclid (Eudoxus)
euclid:V.def.5.work: Elements, Book V, Definition 5 & Proposition 16 (General Theory of Proportion)
euclid:V.def.5.notes: Proves alternation (A:B = C:D => A:C = B:D) required for the Divided Line equality ``|BC| = |CD|`` even for irrational ratios.

euclid:VI.28.author: Euclid
euclid:VI.28.work: Elements, Book VI, Propositions 27–28 (Elliptic Application of Areas & Diorismos)
euclid:VI.28.notes: Exact Euclidean counterpart to Socrates' hypothesis of applying an area with similar defect in Meno 87a.

euclid:VII.def.16.author: Euclid
euclid:VII.def.16.work: Elements, Book VII, Definitions 16–19 (Plane, Solid, Square & Oblong Numbers)
euclid:VII.def.16.notes: Preserves Theaetetus's arithmetic distinction between equilateral square and oblong numbers (147e–148a).

euclid:VIII.11.author: Euclid
euclid:VIII.11.work: Elements, Book VIII, Propositions 11–12 (Means Between Square and Cube Numbers)
euclid:VIII.11.notes: Demonstrates Timaeus 32a–b: one mean proportional between two squares, two means between two cubes.

euclid:X.def.1.author: Euclid (Theaetetus)
euclid:X.def.1.work: Elements, Book X, Definitions 1–4 & Proposition 9 (Commensurability in Length vs. Square)
euclid:X.def.1.notes: Codifies Theaetetus 147d–148b: squares have commensurable sides iff their areas have the ratio of square numbers.

euclid:XIII.13.author: Euclid (Theaetetus)
euclid:XIII.13.work: Elements, Book XIII, Propositions 13–18 (Construction & Exhaustive Comparison of the Five Cosmic Solids)
euclid:XIII.13.notes: Inscribes tetrahedron, octahedron, cube, icosahedron, and dodecahedron in a sphere and proves no sixth regular polyhedron can exist (cf. Timaeus 54d–55c).

proclus:in-euclidem.author: Proclus Diadochus
proclus:in-euclidem.work: In Primum Euclidis Elementorum Librum Commentarii (ed. Friedlein 1873; trans. Morrow 1970)
proclus:in-euclidem.notes: Neoplatonic mathematical synthesis linking Philebus, Republic VI–VII, Meno, Parmenides, and Timaeus to Euclid Book I (geometor/proclus).

proclus:in-timaeum.author: Proclus Diadochus
proclus:in-timaeum.work: In Platonis Timaeum Commentaria, ed. Ernst Diehl, 3 vols. (Leipzig: Teubner, 1903–1906)
proclus:in-timaeum.notes: Preserves Crantor's base-384 integer table and verifies the 34-pitch Timaeus World-Soul scale.

aristotle:anal-post.author: Aristotle
aristotle:anal-post.notes: Engages Meno's paradox and Republic's doctrine of mathematical hypotheses and diagrams (geometor/aristotle).

aristotle:metaphysics.author: Aristotle
aristotle:metaphysics.work: Metaphysica, Books A.6, B.2, M.1–3 (ed. Ross 1924)
aristotle:metaphysics.notes: Primary witness for Plato's doctrine of mathematical intermediates (ta mathēmatika) between Forms and sensibles.

aristotle:de-caelo.author: Aristotle
aristotle:de-caelo.notes: Critiques Timaeus 53c–56c on generating three-dimensional bodies from weightless planar triangles.

heath:greek-math:1921.author: Heath, Sir Thomas Little
heath:greek-math:1921.work: A History of Greek Mathematics, Vol. I: From Thales to Euclid (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1921)
heath:greek-math:1921.locus: Vol. I, Ch. IX ('Plato', pp. 284–315) & pp. 202–212
heath:greek-math:1921.notes: Standard reconstruction of Meno's geometric hypothesis, Theodorus's √3..√17 methods, and the Timaeus scale.

heath:euclid:1926.author: Heath, Sir Thomas Little
heath:euclid:1926.work: The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements, 2nd ed., 3 vols. (Cambridge University Press, 1926)
heath:euclid:1926.notes: Exhaustive commentary reconciling all 21 Plato citations in geometor/euclid and geometor/elements.

taylor:timaeus:1928.author: Taylor, A. E.
taylor:timaeus:1928.work: A Commentary on Plato's Timaeus (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1928)
taylor:timaeus:1928.notes: Detailed mathematical analysis of the World-Soul harmonic intervals and cosmic polyhedra.

cornford:timaeus:1937.author: Cornford, Francis Macdonald
cornford:timaeus:1937.work: Plato's Cosmology: The Timaeus of Plato Translated with a Running Commentary (London: Routledge, 1937)
cornford:timaeus:1937.notes: Clarifies the band construction of the Circles of the Same and the Different and the planar triangle assemblies.

pacioli:divina:1509.author: Pacioli, Fra Luca
pacioli:divina:1509.notes: Renaissance synthesis of Timaeus 53c–56c and Euclid Book XIII (geometor/pacioli).

hoenen:noetica:1952.author: Hoenen, Petrus H. J., S.J.
hoenen:noetica:1952.work: De Noetica Geometriae: Origine Theoriae Cognitionis (Rome: Analecta Gregoriana 63, 1954)
hoenen:noetica:1952.notes: Scholastic-noetic analysis of Meno 82b–85b, Republic VI–VII, and Laws V 737e (geometor/hoenen).

knorr:evolution:1975.author: Knorr, Wilbur Richard
knorr:evolution:1975.work: The Evolution of the Euclidean Elements: A Study of the Theory of Incommensurable Magnitudes and Its Significance for Early Greek Geometry (Dordrecht: Reidel, 1975)
knorr:evolution:1975.notes: Definitive modern study of Theodorus's stopping-point at √17 and Theaetetus's theory of quadratic powers.
